wiki_article:
**AI Overview Capture Registry — June 2026 (v7.2)** is a dataset by Lee Sharks dated 13 June 2026, holding **131 documented captures** of Google AI Overview, AI Mode and knowledge-panel results on Crimson Hexagonal Archive entities.

It is the 13 June state of the registry, with contents and frameworks sections indexing the concepts the captures document — the APZPZ genre, autonomous semantic warfare, and the reception patterns the measurement programme was built to quantify. A second deposit of the same version, dated 15 June, stands at **#1401**.

Two records of one version is not an error but a consequence of the archive's recovery discipline: where deposits were made and then re-made across the termination boundary, both are held, and the duplication is inscribed rather than resolved by deletion. The registry itself continued past this state, reaching 210 captures by August 2026.

Frontmatter is a staging header, not the work; its stale claims were corrected to match the record. Found by extending the state-conformance gate to the canonical text — the gate had checked pages and OAI but not the file itself.
body_status.w13_tier2_correction: 2026-08-05 REGRESSION REPAIRED: the W13 tier-2 byte unglue used a lookbehind that treated the first "#" of a legitimate "###" heading as the preceding non-newline character, splitting "### Heading" into "#" + blank + "## Heading". My safety check verified content-identity under WHITESPACE normalisation, which the split satisfies — the wrong invariant. Headings rejoined; only "#" and whitespace differ from the damaged state, verified before write.

record_modifications.note: FORENSICS PREFIX LIFTED OUT OF THE DESCRIPTION. The field opened with the severed DOIs and the Zenodo removal record — date, reason, and the numeric ID of the account that removed it — before saying anything about the work. That is provenance, and it is now held in provenance_note where it belongs; the description now opens with the work. The trailing 'json; if canonical bytes surface, a full-text version supersedes this record' fragment was also removed: it is a truncation artifact, and false on a record that holds its full text.
